misconception_pool.misconception: Resting your wrists firmly on a padded gel wrist rest while actively typing prevents carpal tunnel syndrome and tendon strain.
misconception_pool.fact: Pressing wrists against a pad while typing compresses the carpal tunnel; float your wrists neutral and use rests only during pauses.

misconception_pool.misconception: Typing harder and stretching aching fingers backward immediately relieves tendon inflammation during a long programming session.
misconception_pool.fact: Forceful stretching irritates inflamed tendons; stop typing right away, rest the hand in a neutral position, and apply a cold pack.

misconception_pool.misconception: Sitting close to a bright monitor in a dark room sharpens text contrast and reduces eye fatigue during late-night coding.
misconception_pool.fact: High screen glare against a dark room forces your pupils to adjust constantly; match screen brightness to even ambient room lighting.

misconception_pool.misconception: Sharing a screenshot of your full desktop or code editor online is safe as long as no password box is open on screen.
misconception_pool.fact: Full screenshots often leak API keys, local file paths, browser tabs, or personal data that should be cropped or redacted first.

misconception_pool.misconception: Computer programming began only after silicon microprocessors were invented in California research labs.
misconception_pool.fact: Ada Lovelace documented algorithmic process execution on paper long before electronic computers existed.

misconception_pool.misconception: Ada Lovelace wrote the first computer program by testing her code directly on a running electronic computer in the 1840s.
misconception_pool.fact: Lovelace wrote her Bernoulli number algorithm in 1843 for Charles Babbage's mechanical Analytical Engine, which was never completed.

misconception_pool.misconception: High-level languages like FORTRAN and COBOL run directly on the processor without being translated into machine code first.
misconception_pool.fact: Processors execute only binary machine instructions, so a compiler or interpreter must translate high-level code before it can run.

misconception_pool.misconception: Grace Hopper invented the term debugging purely as a metaphor because early computer programs had no actual physical hardware bugs.
misconception_pool.fact: In 1947, operators taped an actual moth into the Harvard Mark II logbook after removing it from a relay that caused a malfunction.

misconception_pool.misconception: Object-oriented programming was invented in the 1990s specifically to build interactive web pages with Java and JavaScript.
misconception_pool.fact: Object-oriented concepts originated in the 1960s with Simula 67 and matured in the 1970s with Smalltalk long before the World Wide Web.
